advanced reader of this commentary should have beside it. Judge each text on what it says in its own place, not
on resemblance of a word. Weigh at least:

- paralel: the same figure, scene or story told in the other scripture;
- motif: a shared image, formula, liturgical act or ethical motif without a shared story;
- karsi_anlati: the Qur'an tells it differently, corrects or answers it; the difference is the point;

you rely on it. Discovery is memory-only: the later verifier will open the actual texts and check your claims.

Include every candidate meeting this standard. There is no target list length. Strong means a direct,
specific correspondence, including a secondary feature developed in the prose. Medium means a specific
correspondence with an explicit interpretive bridge. Weak means a plausible, specific connection whose
uncertainty you identify; it still cannot be generic. Counter-narrative is a relationship kind, not weaker

## Frozen commentary (Turkish)

Bu görüntü gün boyunca dönen göğü gösterir. Dördüncü ayetteki "yevm" kelimesi, güneşin doğuşundan batışına kadar geçen süredir: {ar:اليوم مقداره من طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها, tr:el-yevmü mikdâruhû min tulû'i'ş-şemsi ilâ gurûbihâ, gloss:günün uzunluğu güneşin doğuşundan batışına kadardır, source:"ي و م,B001"}. Altıncı ayetteki "müstakîm" kelimesinin ailesinde bu günün ortası vardır: {ar:قام قائم الظهيرة إذا قامت الشمس وكاد الظل يعقل, tr:kâme kâimü'z-zahîre izâ kâmeti'ş-şemsü ve kâde'z-zıllü ya'kılu, gloss:öğle vakti dikildi, yani güneş tepede durdu ve gölge neredeyse yok oldu, source:"ق و م,B017"}. Aynı an bir terazinin dengeye gelmesi olarak da anlatılır: {ar:قام ميزان النهار فاعتدل, tr:kâme mîzânü'n-nehâri fa'tedel, gloss:gündüzün terazisi dikilip dengeye geldi, source:"ق و م,B017"}. Birinci ayetteki "bism" kelimesinin ailesinde ufuktan biraz yükselmiş bir hilal vardır: {ar:سماوة الهلال شخصه إذا ارتفع عن الأفق شيئا, tr:semâvetü'l-hilâli şahsuh, gloss:hilalin semâvesi, ufuktan biraz yükseldiğinde görünen şeklidir, source:"س م و,B002"}. Gök de bu ailedendir: {ar:السماء كل ما علاك فأظلك, tr:es-semâü küllü mâ alâke fe-ezalleke, gloss:sema, üstünde durup sana gölge eden her şeydir, source:"س م و,B004"}. Yedinci ayetteki "en'amte" kelimesinin ailesinde Ay'ın konaklarından biri vardır: {ar:والنعائم منزل من منازل القمر, tr:ve'n-neâimü menzilün min menâzili'l-kamer, gloss:neâim, Ay'ın konaklarından biridir, source:"ن ع م,B007"}. İkinci ayetteki "âlem" kelimesi bütün bunları içine alan gök küresidir: {ar:العالم اسم للفلك وما يحويه, tr:el-âlemü ismün li'l-feleki ve mâ yahvîh, gloss:âlem, gök küresinin ve içindekilerin adıdır, source:"ع ل م,B003"}.

Bu görüntüde "müstakîm" kelimesi kendi anlamının yanında bir an da hissettirir. Güneş tepede dikildiğinde gölge ne sağa ne sola düşer ve gündüzün terazisi dengeye gelir. Yolun dosdoğru olması ile öğlenin dengesi kelimenin ailesinde yan yana durur. Aynı kök hem eğilmeyen yolu hem de gölgesi düşmeyen anı adlandırır. Bu, kökün kendi içinde kurduğu bir bağdır ve yorumu buradan öteye taşımak gerekmez. Görüntünün asıl ağırlığı ise başka bir yerdedir. Birinci ayetteki "Allah" adının ailesinde güneşin de bir adı vardır: {ar:والإلاهة الشمس سميت بذلك لأن قوما كانوا يعبدونها, tr:ve'l-ilâhetü'ş-şems, sümmiyet bi-zâlike li-enne kavmen kânû ya'büdûnehâ, gloss:ilâhe güneştir; bir kavim ona taptığı için bu adı almıştır, source:"ء ل ه,B001"}. Beşinci ayetin {ar:إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ, tr:iyyâke na'büdü, gloss:yalnız sana kulluk ederiz, source:1:5} sözü, kulluğu gökte yükselip batan bu ışıklardan ayırır.

Kur'an bu ayrımı açıkça yapar: {ar:لَا تَسْجُدُوا۟ لِلشَّمْسِ وَلَا لِلْقَمَرِ وَٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَهُنَّ إِن كُنتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ, tr:lâ tescüdû li'ş-şemsi ve lâ li'l-kameri vescüdû lillâhillezî halakahünne in küntüm iyyâhü ta'büdûn, gloss:güneşe de aya da secde etmeyin; eğer yalnız O'na kulluk ediyorsanız, onları yaratan Allah'a secde edin, source:41:37}. Bu ayetteki "iyyâhü ta'büdûn" sözü, surenin "iyyâke na'büdü" sözünün üçüncü şahısla söylenmiş halidir. İbrahim'in sahnesinde gök, yol ve sapma birlikte görülür. Gece onu örtünce bir yıldız görür ve "bu benim Rabbim" der. Yıldız batınca {ar:لَآ أُحِبُّ ٱلْءَافِلِينَ, tr:lâ uhibbü'l-âfilîn, gloss:batanları sevmem, source:6:76} der. Doğmakta olan ayı görünce aynı şeyi söyler. Ay batınca şöyle der: {ar:لَئِن لَّمْ يَهْدِنِى رَبِّى لَأَكُونَنَّ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ, tr:le-in lem yehdinî rabbî le-ekûnenne mine'l-kavmi'd-dâllîn, gloss:Rabbim beni yola iletmezse, ben de mutlaka yolunu yitirmiş kavimden olurum, source:6:77}. Bu cümlede Fâtiha'nın "Rab", "hidayet", "kavm" ve "dâllîn" kelimeleri bir arada geçer. İbrahim ufuktan yükselen bir şekli, yani "semâvetü'l-hilâl"i görür, onu Rab sanar ve batışını görünce yönünü yitirme tehlikesini fark eder. Güneşte de aynı şey olur. Sonunda yüzünü göklerin ve yerin yaratıcısına çevirir: {ar:إِنِّى وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِىَ لِلَّذِى فَطَرَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ حَنِيفًۭا, tr:innî veccehtü vechiye lillezî fatara's-semâvâti ve'l-arda hanîfâ, gloss:ben yüzümü, hanif olarak, gökleri ve yeri yaratana çevirdim, source:6:79}. Hüdhüd, Süleyman'a güneşe tapan bir halkı haber verir: {ar:يَسْجُدُونَ لِلشَّمْسِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ, tr:yescüdûne li'ş-şemsi min dûnillâh, gloss:Allah'ı bırakıp güneşe secde ediyorlar, source:27:24}. Ardından sonucu söyler: {ar:فَصَدَّهُمْ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ فَهُمْ لَا يَهْتَدُونَ, tr:fe-saddehüm ani's-sebîli fe-hüm lâ yehtedûn, gloss:onları yoldan alıkoydu, onlar da yolu bulamıyorlar, source:27:24}. Güneşe tapmak burada yoldan alıkonmak olarak anlatılır. Aynı haberde bu halkı bir kadının yönettiği söylenir: {ar:إِنِّى وَجَدتُّ ٱمْرَأَةًۭ تَمْلِكُهُمْ, tr:innî vecedtü'mraeten temlikühüm, gloss:onlara hükmeden bir kadın buldum, source:27:23}. Ay'ın konakları ise bir hesap için yaratılmıştır: {ar:وَٱلْقَمَرَ نُورًۭا وَقَدَّرَهُۥ مَنَازِلَ لِتَعْلَمُوا۟ عَدَدَ ٱلسِّنِينَ وَٱلْحِسَابَ, tr:ve'l-kamera nûran ve kaddarahû menâzile li-ta'lemû adede's-sinîne ve'l-hisâb, gloss:ayı bir ışık yaptı ve yılların sayısını ve hesabı bilesiniz diye ona konaklar biçti, source:10:5}. Hilaller de birer vakit işaretidir: {ar:يَسْـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلْأَهِلَّةِ ۖ قُلْ هِىَ مَوَٰقِيتُ لِلنَّاسِ وَٱلْحَجِّ, tr:yes'elûneke ani'l-ehille, kul hiye mevâkîtü li'n-nâsi ve'l-hacc, gloss:sana hilalleri soruyorlar; de ki: onlar insanlar ve hac için vakit ölçüleridir, source:2:189}. Mağara sahnesinde güneş gençlerin üzerinden sağa ve sola kayar ve ayet şöyle biter: {ar:مَن يَهْدِ ٱللَّهُ فَهُوَ ٱلْمُهْتَدِ, tr:men yehdillâhü fe-hüve'l-mühted, gloss:Allah kimi yola iletirse yolu bulan odur, source:18:17}.

  cmd: "cat > enrichment/bible/work/s001/discovery/pilot1-20261005/sec8/luna/list.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.1.14	celestial lights mark seasons and years	The commentary cites crescents as time markers and lunar stations for calculation; Genesis assigns the heavenly lights to seasons, days, and years, placing calendrical order in the created sky.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.104.19	moon for appointed times; sun's setting	The commentary defines yawm by sunrise and sunset and adds lunar stations; this verse assigns the moon to appointed times and says the sun knows its setting, joining both clocks in one creation hymn.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.1.5	sun's daily circuit	The commentary's yawm runs from sunrise to sunset; Ecclesiastes depicts the sun rising, setting, and returning to its place, making the repeated daytime circuit explicit.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.19.5	sun crossing the heavens	The commentary pictures the sky turning through the day; the psalm's sun runs across the heavens from one end to the other, adding a full-circuit image to the sunrise-to-sunset gloss.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Josh.10.13	sun halted before setting	The commentary's Arabic root gloss pictures the sun standing at noon; Joshua says the sun stood in mid-heaven and did not hurry to set, presenting a miraculous extension of daylight.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Amos.8.9	noon turned to darkness	The commentary's gloss places the sun upright at noon with almost no shadow; Amos reverses that image by making the sun set at noon and darkening the day as a judgment sign.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Mark.15.33	darkness at the sixth hour	The commentary's root gloss evokes a high, unobscured midday sun; Mark places darkness over the land from the sixth hour, a contrary noon image in a distinct scene.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.4.18	path shining toward full day	The commentary links the straight-path image to the sun at its noon height; Proverbs pictures the righteous path as dawn light growing brighter until full day, joining ethical direction to the day's light.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.121.5	overhead shade	The commentary's source gloss describes the sky as what is above and shades a person; this psalm calls the LORD one's shade at the right hand, transferring the shelter image to divine protection.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.121.6	protection from sun and moon	The commentary says the cave's sun shifts aside from the sleepers; the psalm promises that sun will not strike by day nor moon by night under God's keeping, a close image of shelter from celestial exposure.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.81.4	new moon and feast day	The commentary cites the crescent as a time marker for people and pilgrimage; the psalm sounds a trumpet at the new moon and full moon for a feast, showing lunar phases setting communal worship time.
strong	tevrat	motif	Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 2:8	witnesses identify the crescent	The commentary's source gloss describes a crescent just risen above the horizon; the Mishnah has Rabban Gamliel use moon-shaped images to question witnesses, showing how visible lunar form could govern the calendar.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 43:6-8	moon phases mark seasons and festivals	The commentary names lunar stations as aids to reckoning and crescents as time signs; Sirach describes the moon's phases as markers of seasons and feast days, an explicit Jewish calendrical parallel.
medium	tevrat	motif	1 Enoch 73:1-11	ordered lunar phases	The commentary evokes a crescent and a station of the moon; 1 Enoch lays out the moon's recurring phases and course, giving a Jewish astronomical account of the ordered lunar cycle without equating its system with the commentary's term.
medium	tevrat	karsi_anlati	Jubilees 6:32-38	364-day solar calendar	The commentary cites lunar stations for counting years and crescents for marking times; Jubilees prescribes a 364-day year and warns against lunar reckoning that disrupts the seasons, a specific Jewish calendar counter-position.
weak	incil	karsi_anlati	SBLGNT:Gal.4.10	days, months, seasons, and years	The commentary treats the crescent and lunar stations as useful measures of time; Paul places observance of days, months, seasons, and years within the Galatians' return to bondage, a contrasting Christian evaluation, though he does not name the crescent.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.31.26	sun shining and moon in splendor	The commentary's Abraham says he does not love the setting luminaries; Job describes seeing the bright sun or moon walking in splendor, then tests whether that sight entices him to worship.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.31.27	hand-kissing as worship	The commentary contrasts worship of the sun with worship of God alone; Job names a secretly enticed heart and a hand kissing the mouth as the gesture of astral devotion.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.31.28	denial of the God above	The commentary's Abraham turns from setting lights to the Creator of heaven and earth; Job says worship of the sun or moon would deny the God above, making the theological judgment explicit.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.4.19	sun, moon, and host of heaven	The commentary distinguishes worship of the rising and setting lights from worship of their Creator; Deuteronomy warns Israel not to be drawn into bowing to the sun, moon, stars, or heavenly host.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.17.3	serving the sun or moon	The commentary cites the prohibition on prostrating to sun and moon; Deuteronomy treats serving either luminary or the host of heaven as covenantal apostasy, giving the prohibition a legal setting.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.8.16	men bowing to the eastern sun	The commentary describes people prostrating to the sun instead of God; Ezekiel sees men with their backs to the temple and faces east, bowing to the sun, making the bodily reversal concrete.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:2Kgs.23.5	organized solar and lunar cult	The commentary's sun-worshippers have a public cult; Kings reports priests burning incense to the sun, moon, constellations, and all the host of heaven, supplying an Israelite institutional example.

strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Amos.5.26	star carried as a god's image	The commentary's Abraham sees a star and rejects a setting object as lord; WLC Amos names a star of a god among Israel's cult objects, showing the same kind of celestial body made an object of worship.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Acts.7.42	the host of heaven worshipped	The commentary says sun-worship kept a people from the path; Stephen says God turned away and gave Israel over to worship the host of heaven, linking astral worship with divine abandonment.
strong	incil	yorum_gelenegi	SBLGNT:Acts.7.43	star of Rephan	The commentary's Abraham refuses a celestial body as lord; Stephen revoices the star-god tradition of Amos as the star of Rephan and connects the cult to exile, showing a Christian reception of Israel's astral-idolatry text.

medium	tevrat	paralel	Jubilees 12:16-21	Abram observes celestial signs	The commentary's Abraham tests a star, moon, and sun and turns to their Creator; Jubilees presents Abram studying celestial signs before recognizing sun, moon, and stars as subject to the Lord, a related Abraham tradition whose concern is prognostication rather than a sequence of rival lords.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.14.22	Abraham names heaven's Creator	The commentary ends Abraham's sky scene with his face turned to the Creator of heaven and earth; in Genesis Abraham swears by the Most High, maker of heaven and earth, giving a close Abrahamic statement of allegiance.

medium	tevrat	karsi_anlati	WLC:Gen.15.6	Abraham trusts the LORD	The commentary's Abraham seeks guidance after the moon sets and turns to the Creator; Genesis says Abraham believes the LORD in the star-promise scene, placing trust in God rather than in the lights themselves.
